item.title: Re: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
This is giving me a lot of Class of '76 vibes (I'd suggest checking out more of those articles), but this isn't the clearest idea to read. The elevator pitch is supposed to be the short snappy blurb to get people interested, but it is bigger than the central narrative where you're supposed to explain the story you want to tell here. Maybe focus on the MTF that gets trapped in the book is my suggestion?

I'd suggest rewriting the concept a bit to make it more concise, It's an interesting concept but it needs refining.

item.title: Re: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded: I have made some changes now what do you think?

item.title: Re: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
1) There are plenty of stories, between trepanning, lobotomy, and the various eugenics tactics, so there should be plenty of fun in that regard. There should be plenty of additional stories in a universe where people sacrifice to eldritch horrors.

2) The basic problem is that you delve too much into the hook and not enough into the photobooks themselves. There are no mechanics on how it works, how a killer is determined for the person in question, not even if it is permanent or temporary. You have an interesting idea, but the item itself just isn't described to any degree. Heck, there's not even a lot of history given on it, and what little history there is doesn't really set it up.

3) In that regard, you have way too much hook. In fact, most of the central narrative is nothing but hook. Summarize it and add it to the hook section, and then go back and build your central narrative. You've got a great hook; you just need some actual details.

item.title: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
Idea Post:

Seeking Greenlights: Primarily Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror a lot, Drama/Emotional a good deal, History a little.

Page Layout (Optional): Basic special containment procedures and description followed by how it was obtained, then testing logs, and finally incident reports (maybe). I also want to provide a record of an MTF who has been trapped in the book.

Elevator Pitch: Photobook slash journal used by a former researcher working at an asylum (the early ’50s to ’70s) studying primarily murderous and violent patients. People who place a photo in the book begin to have their memories and their personalities overwritten with psychotic patients.

Central Narrative: I want to highlight the malpractices and the sickening practices of asylums that studied the brains of ‘psychotic’ individuals. Reports of weird experiments have always been rumored and very few reports survive from these places because some of these acts were perpetrated by leading scientists who used this research to better our understanding of psychology. There are even reports of human sacrifices and brutal use of pagan rituals and some real dark sh. Whether or not these are real stories says what if they were really basically. Anyone who places their photo into the book will be able to have their own personality imprinted on another person, however, these people claim they have been taken to an asylum far away from where they were brutally experimented on. Those who went in perfectly sound in mind frequently return with broken minds. There is an eighty percent chance that within the first hour if the person whose photo is removed their personality will stop being overwritten however for every hour it decreases by twenty percent. And for every hour less and less of the subject's sanity is retained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is unique in my opinion are the stories the imprinted patients can tell to people, the horrors they experienced, and how it happened.

Additional Notes: I know there are no factual claims to the horrors of such asylums in real life but I just want to tell the story, please don’t come to tell me why it isn't factual. It's SCP it ain’t meant to be factual it's meant to be fun!
